name: _linalg_solve_ex
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::_linalg_solve_ex(Tensor A, Tensor B, *, bool left=True, bool check_errors=False) -> (Tensor result, Tensor LU, Tensor pivots, Tensor info). All supplied registered schema strings, listed verbatim: [1] aten::_linalg_solve_ex(Tensor A, Tensor B, *, bool left=True, bool check_errors=False) -> (Tensor result, Tensor LU, Tensor pivots, Tensor info); [2] aten::_linalg_solve_ex.result(Tensor A, Tensor B, *, bool left=True, bool check_errors=False, Tensor(a!) result, Tensor(b!) LU, Tensor(c!) pivots, Tensor(d!) info) -> (Tensor(a!) result, Tensor(b!) LU, Tensor(c!) pivots, Tensor(d!) info). The original Gems pytest owns the full contract: it defines the overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation behavior, and this one representative signature is not exclusive; never remove tests or adapt reference behavior to fit it. Semantics derived from the tests: for A of shape (batch..., n, n), left=True takes B of shape (batch..., n, m) and solves AX = B, while left=False takes B of shape (batch..., m, n) and solves XA = B. It returns the four-tuple (result, LU, pivots, info), where result has B's shape, LU carries the (batch..., n, n) factorization with 1-based permutation pivots of shape (batch..., n), and info has A's batch shape (an empty tuple for an unbatched A) with a nonzero entry for singular lanes. A must have rank >= 2 and B is required; batch axes broadcast, and info follows A's batch shape rather than the broadcast result shape. The default overload mutates nothing and returns freshly allocated tensors, while the .result overload writes into caller-provided out buffers, mutates them and returns those same buffer objects, which the pytest additionally checks for strided views, guard regions and view-geometry preservation; that conditional out-parameter behavior is exercised by the tests rather than expressed here. Singular input is reported through info, and check_errors=True raises RuntimeError instead of returning it; the unsupported-dtype rejection cases are measured only on the NVIDIA vendor path and remain scoped to that backend (RuntimeError/TypeError there), while invalid shapes are rejected with RuntimeError. Vector right-hand sides are accepted only for the left=True form.
